text:
nik: Quick RFC follow-up: we need a clear boundary between SLA-weighted admission and general burst admission. Proposal: a lightweight policy evaluator (no new scaler) that enforces per-tenant SLA bands and delegates capacity changes to the existing autoscaler.

maria: thin evaluator = admission gate + counters only? prefer not to add another control loop.

sam: model SLA as token-buckets per tenant so runtime stays simple.

lee: need deterministic degrade: when tokens drain, either 1) soft reject with Retry-After + UX guidance, or 2) auto-fallback to cheaper model variants (tenant opt-in).

nik: example policy: sla_weight, token_bucket {capacity, refill_per_min}, fallback_order list. Also include adaptive refill based on observed p95 with EWMA smoothing.

maria: agree on adaptive refill but avoid oscillation; min floor for refill.

sam: prefer control-plane proxy for the evaluator (dry-run rollout, audit logs).

lee: require "sla_band_depleted" events + tags (tenant_id, action) for SRE alerts.

infra-bot: deploy: autoscaler-proxy v0.9 canaryed in cluster-b.

nik: testing: build a sim harness to replay traces and compute: rejections, fallback_calls, tokens_used, cost_delta. Keep evaluator pure so dry-run equals live decisions.

maria: I'll own the sim harness; will produce CSV report.

sam: I'll prototype proxy API + YAML schema.

lee: I'll spec metrics and 429 error payload (Retry-After, X-Redwood-Fallback-URL).

nik: logging: publish ndjson decisions to kafka topic sla-policy-decisions.v1. infra confirmed topic.

infra-bot: notice: topic sla-policy-decisions.v1 created (retention=14d).

nik: follow-ups: maria sim PR, sam proxy sketch, lee metrics PR. Post links here. Thanks! :raised_hands:
